label: Third original token after a sequence opening with 11, z1, 1z or m1
predicate: (t == 2) & (((prev_tok == tok("1")) & isin(prev2_tok, [tok("1"), tok("z"), tok("m")])) | ((prev_tok == tok("z")) & (prev2_tok == tok("1"))))
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost always at step 2 (the third input token; a few weak activations at step 3), and only when the first two tokens form one of a small set of bigrams: 11, z1, 1z (strong; precision 1.0 for these three) and m1 (weak, about 0.0-0.1 of max). Other X1 openings (x1, s1, 01, p1, j1, f1) give rare weak activations. It is strongest for the 11 opening (activations up to max, especially when the third token is n), mid-range for z1 and 1z. It does not fire on zz, fz, mz or f1 openings in general, and never fires in the delimiter or copy phase. Dev: P 0.94, R 0.82, F1 0.875, mass recall 0.94.

dev_scores.predicate: (t == 2) & (((prev_tok == tok("1")) & isin(prev2_tok, [tok("1"), tok("z"), tok("m")])) | ((prev_tok == tok("z")) & (prev2_tok == tok("1"))))

issues: Core claims hold. Phase: all activation mass is in the original phase, with 0 actives at the delimiter and in the copy phase. By step: 97.7% of mass is at t=2 and 2.3% at t=3. Sub-predicates at t=2 on dev: 11 has P=1.0 and 54.7% of mass, 1z has P=1.0 and 18.1%, z1 has P=1.0 and 19.9%. m1 has P=0.76 but only 1.4% of mass, so it is weak, as claimed. zz, fz and mz all have P=0. f1 has P=0.21. Magnitude peaks after 11 with n third: 25 steps, P=1.0, 3.3% of mass, so a high mean activation.

The explanation misdescribes one class of misses. The leftover activations after other X1 openings are not scattered: they concentrate on third token n. (t==2)&(prev_tok=='1')&(in_tok=='n') with prev2 outside {1,z,m} has P=0.42 and makes up about 190 of the ~500 missed steps (p1n, s1n and x1n at ~0.1 of max). in_tok n has a 3.6x lift overall.

The t=3 activations (5.5% of active steps, 2.3% of mass) are also systematic. Every one has 11 at steps 1-2: (t==3)&prev=='1'&prev2=='1' has recall equal to all t=3 activity and P=0.24. The explanation only calls them 'a few weak activations at step 3'.
Most false positives are m1 followed by p, e or o, i.e. m1 is only partly included.

These gaps are small in mass. Adding the X1n clause gives test F1 0.870 vs 0.864 and mass recall 0.977 vs 0.937. That is a small gain, so the label and predicate stand, apart from the wording about the leftover X1 activations.
